detection_findings: Both scanners produced identical canonical target sets, finding identities, category counts and failure counts on filesystem and Git.
RNC-MOD-v14 added no RNC Lab true positives, removed none, and introduced no different false positives or unverified evidence.
performance_findings: Filesystem is effectively tied in the primary order (+0.8%) and modestly slower for the mod in the reverse-order control.
Gitleaks is materially faster on Git history and both legacy load workloads in both orders.
The order-balanced mean shows the mod at +7.2% filesystem, +91.1% Git, +28.7% x5 and +35.5% x10 versus Gitleaks.
The mod uses more peak memory on the load profiles and more scanner CPU on the loads.
assessment.scope_limit: This is not evidence that RNC-MOD-v14 is universally worse; it may target detection gaps outside the RNC Lab corpus. Within the requested scope it yields no measured accuracy gain and a clear throughput regression on Git and loads.

reverse_order_equivalent.note: Reverse-order runs produced identical target sets and finding signatures.

benchmark_environment.description: contended developer workstation; functional and preliminary timing

environment.contention: DEV developer workstation; not release evidence

recommendations: Use Gitleaks 8.25.0-local as the performance and parity reference for these four RNC Lab workloads.
Treat RNC-MOD-v14 as a feature candidate, not a drop-in faster replacement.
If the v14-specific rules matter, run a targeted corpus/rule comparison and profile its startup/rules path.
Do not certify precision/F1; the negative oracle is non-exhaustive.
Do not treat these DEV measurements as release capacity evidence.
